blocks.text: Austurbane is a style aesthetic and product photography design that emerged in the late 2010s. Coined as a term derived from "austere" and "urbane," it mixes stark minimalism with earthy, upscale sophistication. It is characterized by a sleek, pared-down, modern version of Frasurbane, replacing cluttered intellectual nostalgia with zen-like, clean minimalism.

The typography relies on editorial, elegant, serif fonts utilized alongside vast amounts of whitespace, with shadows and lightning that features dramatic, sharper lighting often casting branch shadows and realistic plants across the frame.

Refractive or prismatic elements are frequently utilized to subtly scatter light, with a color palette that frequently relies on neutral, muted earth tones incorporating black, copper, beige, cream and bronze, along with compositions such as product photography having a curated, highly staged feel, often using geometric isometric angles or strict top-down (flat lay) along with the materials emphasizing high-quality natural, raw materials such as marble, textured granite, rough stone, structured fabrics and organic ceramics.
